value.quote: We show tight tradeoﬀs between the consistency and robustness of ordinal mechanisms
value.note: All main results are consistency and robustness bounds on distortion, i.e. welfare ratios. The polynomial-time remark in Lemma 4.1 is auxiliary and not a main algorithmic result.

C1.reason: The main results are distortion (welfare-ratio) bounds and computation is not studied as a main result, so AL does not apply.

value.quote: some (partial) valuation proﬁle v̂ which also induces the same ordinal proﬁle
value.note: The mechanism's argument is the ordinal ranking profile plus a prediction p. In most results p is a (partial) cardinal valuation profile (CARD). In Theorem 3.1, p is a predicted optimal candidate (OTH: predicted outcome).

C2.2.reason: The rule's argument includes the predicted valuations, as A codes, and in the main Theorem 3.1 also a predicted optimal candidate, which needs OTH.

value.quote_behav: each voter i reports an ordering (or, ranking) ≻vi of the candidates
value.note: Voters take a fixed action in the model by reporting rankings consistent with their valuations. Agents in one-sided matching are treated the same way.

C6.VOT.reason: Under C6, an agent taking a fixed action counts as present, and voters are explicitly said to report rankings, so they are present and non-strategic.
